cases.question: Can I take casual leave for 4 days in a row?

Casual Leave also can't be combined with Earned Leave in the same continuous absence [BP-HR-002 p.2].

The extra details about Earned Leave notice and not combining leave types don't contradict the reference. cases.question: How is leave encashment calculated?
cases.expected_answer: (Monthly basic / 26) x days, max 30 EL days, only at separation.
cases.answer:
Leave encashment under the Leave Policy works as follows:

- Only Earned Leave is encashable, and only at the time of separation. [BP-HR-002 p.3]
- A maximum of 30 days can be encashed. [BP-HR-002 p.3]
- Amount = (monthly basic salary ÷ 26) × number of encashable days. [BP-HR-002 p.3]
- Casual Leave, Sick Leave and Compensatory Off are not encashable. [BP-HR-002 p.3]

For questions about your specific case, contact your HR Business Partner or hr-helpdesk@brightpath.example.
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer has all the key facts from the reference: the formula (monthly basic ÷ 26) × days, a maximum of 30 days, Earned Leave only, and only at separation. The extra details about non-encashable leave types don't contradict the reference.

cases.question: Are weekends counted if I take 6 days of earned leave?
cases.expected_answer: Yes. The sandwich rule applies for EL of 5 or more consecutive working days.
cases.answer:
Yes, if your Earned Leave runs for 5 or more consecutive working days, weekends and public holidays that fall between those days are counted as leave. For example, 6 working days of Earned Leave would count any weekend or holiday in between as leave days. [BP-HR-002 p.2]

For shorter stretches (under 5 working days), intervening weekends and holidays are not counted. [BP-HR-002 p.2]
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer says yes and gives the same 5-or-more consecutive working days threshold as the reference. It adds the sandwich rule's effect on weekends and holidays, plus the under-5-days case, and neither detail contradicts the reference.
